increments.title: The raise cost, from the report to the raise dialog
increments.goal: Every capability record of the evaluator report carries the cost of raising one instance of that slot including the child selections the raise is obliged to create, and the two surfaces that offer a raise (the category raise dialog and the auto-fill suggestions) show and sort by that number instead of the own cost. A unit like Grave Guard, whose points hang on its mandatory model child, then shows a price where it showed none.
criteria: Every capability record carries the raise cost of the slot in its own field beside `costs` and `totalCosts`: the effective own cost of one instance plus, for every mandatory child of that slot, that child's raise cost times the child's effective minimum count, applied recursively.
The meaning of `costs` and of `totalCosts` is unchanged.

The raise cost reads effective values only: the cost after every cost modifier holding in the current state, and the effective minimum after every modifier on that bound. A cost modifier tied to the force the offer hangs under is reflected in the number — the Necromancer's Army force (`d3af-1add-4e99-b977`), which sets the Grave Guard model cost to 10, reports a raise cost that differs from the Standard force's accordingly.

In an empty `Standard (VC-AB)` force (`e989-15b8-7eb6-9668`) of the definitive-edition Vampire Counts fixture, the offer anchor of `Grave Guard` (`92ee-2ebf-c6c0-71ff`) reports a raise cost of 120 for cost type `ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249`.
A slot with no mandatory children reports the same raise cost as its own cost, so every unit that shows a price today shows the same price after the change.
The raise cost terminates on catalogue data that links in a cycle.

`CategoryUnitAdder` shows the raise cost instead of the own cost, both in the price it prints and in the descending sort of its candidates, in the form it already uses (`+120 pts`) with no `from` prefix and no extra marker.
`AutoFillSuggestions` reads the raise cost for the same offers, in place of the own cost.
Option lists inside a unit (`SelectionConfigurator`, `OptionGroup`) are untouched and still show an option's own cost.
The roster-wide cost totals (`costTotals`), the validation and the displayed cost of a selection already in the list are unchanged; an offer still contributes to no sum.
The raise cost is pinned by tests over real catalogue data, not only over synthetic XML, and the evaluator's E2E scenarios and unit tests stay green.
`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass.

# INC-1 — the raise cost, from the report to the raise dialog

## The number and where it has to come from

`Grave Guard` (`92ee-2ebf-c6c0-71ff`) declares no `<costs>`. Its points hang on the model child `4d29-67e8-1d93-a404` (12 pts) which the unit must hold at least 10 of (`<constraint type="min" scope="parent" value="10" id="4eb4-459b-b01c-766d">`). Raising the unit costs 120. The offer anchor is a LEAF by design (`offer.js`: "Der Anker ist ein Blatt"), so neither `costs` (own cost of one instance = {}) nor `totalCosts` (no instance, no children = {}) can carry that number, and no node for the model child exists under the anchor.

So the raise cost is a **fourth projected view** that has to evaluate a slot that is not in the tree. The child's cost is not a catalogue constant either: `4d29` carries `<modifier type="set" value="10" field="ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249">` gated on `<condition type="instanceOf" scope="force" childId="d3af-1add-4e99-b977">` — under the Necromancer's Army force the same model costs 10, so the raise cost there is 100, not 120. Criterion 3 therefore forces a real modifier evaluation in the context of the force the offer hangs under; reading `def.costs` off the definition graph is not enough.

Both forces carry the `Special` category (`43cc-fc3f-35a7-8d03`) in their `categoryLinks` (`Standard (VC-AB)` line 29306, `Necromancer's Army (VC-AB)` line 29351 of the VC `.cat`), so the Grave Guard offer anchor exists under both.

## The design: detached shadow children, evaluated by the existing modifier machinery

For each slot, walk its **definition** subtree for the children the raise is obliged to create, and for each such child build a **detached node** — a node that carries `parent` and `forceRoot` pointing into the real tree, but which is NEVER pushed into `parent.children`. Nothing that walks `children` (`allNodes`, `realNodes`, `syntheticNodes`, `selectableSlotsOf`, `buildIndex`, `buildCostProjection`, `evaluateConstraints`, `pathOf`) can then reach it: no capability record, no path shift, no constraint result, no violation, no index entry, no `costTotals` contribution. Criterion 10 holds structurally, not by promise.

The detached node's ancestor chain still resolves scopes: `query.js` `resolveSharedFrame` reads `ctx.node.forceRoot` for `scope="force"` and `ctx.node.parent` for `scope="parent"`, and `resolveAncestor` walks `parent`. That is exactly what makes the `instanceOf`-on-force gate of the Grave Guard model cost fire (or not) correctly.

On those nodes run the two steps the anchor post-pass already runs on offer anchors:

1. `extendBaseEffectiveState(effective, shadowNodes)` — seeds base costs, categories and a derivation per limit from the definition (`baseValuesOf`);
2. `applyModifiersOfNodes(shadowNodes, effective, { root, index, categoryIds, diagnostics, budget, primaryCatalogueByForceDefId })` — the same call `applyAnchorPostPass` makes.

Writing into the report's own `EffectiveState` is required, not merely convenient: `applyModifiersOfNodes` passes the same state as `effective` into the query context, and a fresh state would make `ancestor`/`primary-category`/category-scope conditions read empty values off the REAL ancestors. It is free of feedback for the same three reasons `applyAnchorPostPass` documents: the index is finished and only read, the state keys by node OBJECT so a shadow node can never overwrite a real node's value, and the tree is not modified.

Then:

```
raiseCost(node, visited) =
  effective own costs of node                     // per cost type
  + Σ over mandatory children c of node:
        effectiveMin(c) × raiseCost(shadowNodeFor(c), visited ∪ {c})
```

- **effective own costs** = `effective.costEntriesOf(node)` — the same source `buildCostProjection` uses for `costs`, so criterion 5 (no mandatory children ⇒ raise cost equals own cost) is true by construction.
- **mandatory child** = a child definition of the slot's owner definition, reached through `selectionEntryGroup`s and group-typed `entryLink`s exactly as `synthesizeParentScopePhantoms` reaches them (`selectionDefinitionsUnder(ownerDefinitionOf(node))`), whose `limitsOf(childDef)` holds a limit with `kind === ConstraintKind.MIN` and `scope === ScopeKeyword.PARENT`. `DefinitionKind.CATEGORY_LINK` children are skipped — a category is not a selection anyone pays for.
- **effectiveMin(c)** = `effective.limitValue(shadowNode, minLimit.id) ?? minLimit.value`, clamped with `Math.max(0, …)`. Read AFTER the modifier pass, so criterion 3's "effective minimum after every modifier on that bound" holds. Selecting candidates by the presence of a parent-scoped MIN (not by its base value) and then reading the effective bound is what makes both directions right: a bound a modifier lifts from 0 counts, a bound a modifier drops to 0 contributes nothing and stops the recursion there.
- **excluded bounds**: a MIN limit whose `field.kind !== CountedFieldKind.SELECTION_COUNT` (a cost-measured minimum) or whose `isPercent` is true is not a piece count and contributes nothing; document that. Neither occurs parent-scoped in the whfb6 fixture (all 312 `type="min"` constraints of the VC `.cat` are non-percent; the only non-`selections` ones are roster-scoped `limit::…` budget minimums). A bound read as `UNLIMITED` (the `-1` sentinel, already deciphered at read time) contributes nothing.

**Termination on cyclic catalogue data (criterion 6)**: a `visited` set of definition ids carried DOWN THE CURRENT BRANCH, seeded with the slot's own `def.id` and `def.resolved?.id`, and extended with each child's `def.id` and `def.resolved?.id` before descending. A child already on the branch contributes 0 and is not descended into. Per-branch, not global, so the same definition legitimately reached through two different branches is still counted twice.

**Cost of the pass**: memoise the definition-level answer "which children of this definition are mandatory" by `node.def` (object identity) in a `Map` — it is a pure function of `node.def`, and one force offers the same definitions over and over. Where the answer is empty — the overwhelming majority of slots — take the fast path: freeze a copy of the own costs, build no shadow node, apply no modifier. The added work is then proportional to the slots that really do have mandatory children.

## Where each piece lands

**`src/evaluator/evalTree.js`** (this module owns node shape and already owns the "what is a mandatory child" rule) gains two exports:

- `mandatoryChildDefsOf(node)` → `Array<{ def, gates }>`: the mandatory child definitions of a slot with the visibility gates walked to reach them, built on the existing private `selectionDefinitionsUnder(ownerDefinitionOf(node))` + a MIN/`parent` filter. `synthesizeParentScopePhantoms` may keep its own inline filter or be refactored onto this — do not change its behaviour either way.
- `createDetachedChildNode(root, parent, def, gates)` → a node in the same shape as `attachPhantom` produces (`instance: null`, `isPhantom: true`, `isRoot: false`, `isForce: false`, `anchorKind: AnchorKind.MANDATORY_PHANTOM`, `frameId: root.nextFrameId()`, `forceRoot: parent.forceRoot`, `children: []`, `visibilityGates: gates`) that is **deliberately not pushed into `parent.children`**. Its JSDoc must say why in one sentence: everything that reaches nodes reaches them through `children`, so staying out of that array is what keeps the hypothetical slot out of the report.

**`src/evaluator/costProjection.js`** gains a second exported builder:

```js
export function buildRaiseCostProjection(root, effective, { index, categoryIds, budget, primaryCatalogueByForceDefId })
  // → { raiseCostsOf: (node) => Record<string, number> }
```

It walks the same node set as `buildCostProjection` (`for (const child of root.children) …` recursively over `children`), stores one frozen record per node, and returns `NO_COSTS` for a node it does not know. It imports `applyModifiersOfNodes` from `./modifiers.js`, `extendBaseEffectiveState` from `./effectiveState.js` and the two new `evalTree.js` exports. No import cycle arises (`modifiers.js` does not import `costProjection.js`), and `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` carries no intra-evaluator layering rule.

**Diagnostics of the raise-cost pass are collected into a local array and dropped**, and the JSDoc says so and why: the pass evaluates a slot that does not exist in the list, so a finding of it would speak about a node no report path names, and the very same modifier is already diagnosed wherever it applies to a slot that does exist. Merging them would also duplicate findings into the one `diagnostics` list the E2E scenarios read. This is the one place in the engine where a modifier diagnosis is deliberately not forwarded; make that explicit rather than silent.

**`src/evaluator/report.js`**: `extras` gains `raiseCostProjection` (default `null`), and `toCapability` gains, beside `costs` and `totalCosts`:

```js
raiseCosts: raiseCostProjection?.raiseCostsOf(node) ?? costProjection.costsOf(node),
```

The fallback keeps the field present for every capability record even when `buildReport` is called directly (as several unit suites do): without a projection the raise cost degenerates to the own cost, which is exactly its value for a slot with no mandatory children. Document the fallback where the field is documented. `costs` and `totalCosts` are not touched (criterion 2).

**`src/evaluator/evaluator.js`**, section 3 ("Grenzen und Bericht"), AFTER `evaluateConstraints` and `categoryAnchorOccupancies` so the no-feedback ordering reads off the code:

```js
const raiseCostProjection = buildRaiseCostProjection(root, effective, {
  index, categoryIds: resolved.categoryIds, budget, primaryCatalogueByForceDefId,
});
```

passed into `buildReport` through `extras`. The call sits inside the existing `MeasuredPhase.CONSTRAINTS_AND_REPORT` block; no new phase.

**`src/components/editor/CategoryUnitAdder.jsx`**, line ~100:

```js
const costOf = ({ capability }) => capability.raiseCosts?.[costLimitType] ?? 0;
```

One line: it already feeds both the printed price and the descending sort, so criterion 7 is satisfied by that single change. The `points > 0` guard, the `+{points} {costTypeLabel}` form, the absence of any `from` prefix or marker all stay exactly as they are. Correct the module header (line ~16, "Kosten liest `capability.costs`") to name `raiseCosts` and say in one sentence why: the dialog prices a RAISE, and a raise creates the mandatory children with it.

**`src/components/editor/AutoFillSuggestions.jsx`**, line 116:

```js
const cost = capability.raiseCosts?.[costLimitTypeId] ?? 0;
```

The `cost <= 0 || cost > remainingPoints` gate and the descending sort then run on the raise cost, which is the point: a model-priced unit stops being filtered out as "costs nothing" and stops being suggested when it would not actually fit. Update the header sentence about what a suggestion must cost.

**Untouched on purpose**: `SelectionConfigurator`, `OptionGroup`, `UnitSelectionCard`, `PlayUnitDetails`, `PlayMode`, `src/evaluation/` (it passes capability records through unchanged), `costTotals`, `budget.js`, `rosterBudget.js`, `constraints.js`, `violationClassification.js`.

## Documentation to carry with the code

- `costProjection.js` module header: the fourth view, its definition, and that it reads effective values only.
- `report.js` module header (the `SlotCapability` paragraph, ~line 27) and the `toCapability` JSDoc (~line 579): `raiseCosts` beside `costs`/`totalCosts`, plus the `null`-projection fallback.

- `src/components/editor/CLAUDE.md` line 94 (the list of capability fields a case guard-asserts) gains `raiseCosts` — the test-author does that with its cases.

## Language

The evaluator's JSDoc is German throughout and the suite docs say new code comments are English and test titles German. So: write NEW comment blocks and JSDoc in English; when extending an existing German block, add an English sentence rather than rewriting the German around it. `describe`/`it` titles are German, per both suite docs.

## Alternatives rejected

1. **Materialise the mandatory children under offer anchors as real tree nodes.** Uniform and simple, but they would become capability records with their own paths, their own constraint results and their own possible violations — criterion 10 (validation and totals unchanged) forbids it, and `offer.js`'s leaf rule exists to bound the tree's growth.
2. **Compute the number in the surface.** ADR-0034 and the issue both close this: what the catalogue data says is the engine's answer.
3. **Derive it from `totalCosts`.** An offer anchor is a leaf with no instance; both its count and its subtree sum are 0. Nothing to derive from.
4. **Use the existing tree children where they exist (an occupied slot's model child, or its mandatory phantom) and shadow nodes only under offer anchors.** Cheaper for occupied slots, but it makes one rule into two code paths that can disagree — an occupied slot and its own offer anchor would answer differently for the same definition. 5. **Pass `index`/`budget` into `buildReport` and compute the whole thing inside the report layer.** It would make the report layer take the count index and the modifier machinery as inputs. `evaluator.js` already holds both; the projection is handed in finished.
6. **Merge the raise-cost pass's modifier diagnostics into the report's `diagnostics`.** Duplicates findings that are already reported at the real slots and injects messages about slots that are not in the list; would also put the E2E scenarios' diagnostics assertions at risk.
7. **Name the field `raiseCost` (singular).** It is a `Record<costTypeId, number>` like its two neighbours, so `raiseCosts` reads with them.
